Compare peptide descriptors between Conditions

Source: R/pepchem.R
compare_pepchem.Rd

Kruskal-Wallis across all Conditions plus a pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum test for every Condition pair, BH-corrected within each contrast, with the median difference and cliffs_delta() as effect sizes.

Usage

compare_pepchem(
  props,
  level = c("sample", "peptide"),
  properties = NULL,
  fdr = 0.05
)

Arguments

props

Output of pepchem_by_sample().

level

"sample" (default) or "peptide" — see above.

properties

Descriptor columns to test. NULL (default) uses every numeric non-annotation column.

fdr

Significance cut-off applied to the BH-adjusted p-values. Default 0.05.

Value

A data frame with Property, Level, Contrast, Group1, Group2, n1, n2, Median1, Median2, MedianDiff, CliffsDelta, p_value, p_adj and Significant; the overall Kruskal-Wallis table is attached as attr(, "kruskal"). Zero rows when fewer than two Conditions are present.

Details

level selects the unit of analysis, and the two tracks are not interchangeable:

  • "sample" (default) summarises each sample first (median descriptor over its unique sequences) and tests across samples. Samples are the real replicates, so this is the honest test — but it is low-powered: with three replicates per Condition a two-sided Wilcoxon cannot go below p = 0.1, so read the effect sizes, not only the p-values.

  • "peptide" pools the unique sequences of a Condition and tests across peptides. Peptides from one sample are not independent, so this track is pseudo-replicated: its p-values are anti-conservative and it should be read as a description of the repertoire difference (through Cliff's delta), not as inference.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
compare_pepchem(pepchem_by_sample(pep_short), level = "sample")
} # }
